head.h1: Brunch Catering in Dubai — What It Costs and How to Book

opening_paragraph: Brunch catering in Dubai from myCHEF starts at AED 700 per person , quoted to your guest count, menu and service level. A vetted private chef plans the spread, cooks it fresh on site, serves your guests and clears everything away — so the host gets to sit down and enjoy the morning. Share the date, the numbers and the venue, and we come back promptly during our published business hours with a proposal you can read at a glance.

replace_in_block.new_heading: What does brunch catering in Dubai include?
new_paragraphs: It includes the whole event, not just the food: menu design, a professional chef on site, service staff, all cooking, plating, table setup and the cleanup afterwards. A proper brunch caterer dubai host takes the weekend ritual off your plate entirely. We plan the running order around your morning — coffee and juice on arrival, a first savoury wave, then sweet stations and pastries as the table settles. You choose the format, we bring the equipment, chafing dishes, station kit, crockery and linen. As a full brunch catering services dubai team, we also handle the parts nobody enjoys: sourcing fresh produce that morning, keeping hot food hot and cold food cold to Dubai food-safety standards, and leaving your kitchen exactly as we found it.

replace_in_block.new_heading: How much does brunch catering cost in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: Brunch catering cost dubai starts from AED 700 per person and typically runs to around AED 950 per person for a fuller menu with live stations and staffed service. The format drives the number: buffet and drop-off are the lightest on the budget; plated service with dedicated staff sits higher. Curated brunch catering packages dubai begin around AED 1,200, scaling up for larger groups and premium menus. Affordable brunch catering dubai is about matching scope to budget honestly — we will tell you where to spend and where to save. Nobody sells themselves as cheap brunch catering, and we will not pretend a nine-section menu with three manned stations is a budget morning; tell us the ceiling and we build to it, usually by cutting stations, not the food. For a full breakdown, see our Dubai catering price guide , or send your numbers for itemised brunch catering prices dubai.

add_block.new_heading: Brunch catering for weddings, corporate events and parties
new_paragraphs: Yes — the same kitchen scales from an eight-person family table to a two-hundred-guest celebration. A morning-after wedding brunch, a relaxed baby shower, a milestone birthday or a bridal gathering all suit the format beautifully. Corporate brunch catering dubai is one of our busiest requests: launch mornings, team socials, investor breakfasts and networking sessions where a shared table does more for the room than a boardroom lunch ever could. For brunch catering for events dubai on a larger scale, we add live stations and extra service staff so nobody queues. Whatever the occasion, brunch party catering dubai keeps the atmosphere unhurried while the logistics run tightly behind the scenes.

add_block.new_heading: What's on a brunch catering menu in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: Your brunch menu dubai is built around your guests, not off a fixed sheet. A typical spread runs across three layers, and every item is tailored to your taste and dietary needs:
Savoury: shakshuka, eggs cooked to order, smoked-salmon and avocado plates, mini breakfast sliders, saffron-scented grains and a live egg or pancake station.
Sweet: fresh pastries, French toast, waffles, seasonal fruit platters and a dessert corner — where a pastry chef earns their keep.
Drinks: a mocktail bar, fresh-pressed juices, specialty coffee and tea service.

Halal is the default, vegetarian and vegan dishes are flagged item by item, not pushed onto a separate sheet, and we can shape an Arabic, Mediterranean or international brunch food catering dubai spread. Brunch catering packages dubai bundle the menu, chef and service into one clear price, so there are no surprises on the day.

add_block.new_heading: The brunch menu in full, course by course
new_paragraphs: Below is the real shape of a Dubai brunch, not a category list: what lands on arrival, what sits out all morning, what the chef cooks in front of your guests, and what closes the table. Menus are built by chefs who specialise in that cuisine, not adapted from a single house menu, so pick the sections that suit your morning and we build the running order around them. Nothing here is compulsory — a boardroom breakfast might take three sections, a post-wedding villa brunch nine.
On arrival — coffee, karak and juice
The first twenty minutes set the tone, and in Dubai that is a beverage decision as much as a food one. The tea and coffee programme is named, not "a choice of hot drinks":
Speciality roast coffee: flat white, cortado, long black and cappuccino, poured from a manned barista counter
Cold brew: served over ice from the same counter
Arabic coffee (gahwa) with cardamom: poured from the dallah into finjan cups
Karak chai: the Dubai morning default, brewed strong and sweet
Signature tea blends: Earl Grey, Darjeeling, Moroccan mint, oud and saffron-rose
Herbal infusions: caffeine-free options for the table
Matcha and beetroot latte: the wellness end of the drinks list
Freshly squeezed orange juice and watermelon juice
Classic lemonade and berry fruit drink
Infused water station: still and sparkling water alongside

Every continental spread opens here, and six to ten items is the usual count. Pastry is the one section where the difference between a bought-in tray and a baked-that-morning basket is obvious to everybody at the table.
Mini flavoured croissants: caramel and pistachio
Assorted artisan danishes and croissants: the mixed basket, sized by persons served
Mini muffins: feta and olive, or raspberry and almond
Assorted bread station: white, whole wheat and sourdough
Sausage rolls: made with chicken or beef sausage
The cold table — labneh, cheese and preserves
The section a Dubai host notices first, because it is where a Levantine table and a continental one meet. Six to nine items is normal, and it is near-universal on both spreads.
Labneh: strained yoghurt, olive oil, warm pita alongside
Shanklish: aged cheese rolled in zaatar, with tomato and onion
Makdous: baby aubergines cured with walnut and pepper
Olives and fresh vegetables with warm pita
Premium French cheeses and cold cuts
Chicken mortadella and cheese sandwich in ciabatta

This is the section that separates a 2026 brunch from a 2015 one, and it travels well because everything is portioned into its own glass or jar — which is also why it suits a boxed or drop-off morning.
Black chia bowl: coconut milk base
Açaí bowl: granola, peanut butter and fruit
Green morning bowl: spinach, avocado and seeds
Four to six items, and every Dubai brunch menu we read carried one. Seasonal means seasonal — the chef names what is at its peak that week instead of substituting quietly.
Fruit in Cup Box: single-hand format for a grab-and-go counter
Individual fresh exotic fruit salad: honey cinnamon yoghurt
If a caterer is going to be judged on one section in this city, it is this one. Six to nine items is the working spread, and the names are written the way the kitchen says them.
Foul Medammas: slow-cooked fava beans, lemon, olive oil, cumin
Balila: warm fava beans and chickpeas
Shakshouka: eggs baked in spiced tomato
Arabic shakshuka: the Levantine version, served in the pan
Hummus fatteh: hummus, toasted bread, pine nuts, yoghurt
Eggs your way: cooked to order at the pass
Falafel: fried to order, with tahini
Lahm bi ajine: minced meat flatbread
Emirati Fuala — the local heritage table
Fuala is served morning and evening, and it is a distinct skillset, not a Levantine chef improvising. Six to ten items, presented on brass, traditional or modern as you prefer.
Balaleet: saffron vermicelli with omelette laid over it
Chebab: Emirati pancakes with date syrup
The familiar half of the hot line, re-specified for a halal table: turkey bacon, beef bacon, chicken sausage and turkey ham throughout, not pork. Six to ten items holds a chafing line without gaps.
Sweet potato rosti with poached eggs
Croque-monsieur: gruyere cheese, smoked sausage, pickled red onion
A named section on its own, not folded into "international". Four to seven items, and it is the section a South Indian specialist changes completely.

The backbone of any drop-off or grab-and-go morning, and the format most offices ask for — pre-wrapped, labelled per guest, eaten one-handed. Boxed sandwich catering dubai buyers ask for by name is this section, sized by persons served, not by tray.
Smoked salmon bagel: pickled cucumber, red onion, mayonnaise
Free-range egg roll: turkey bacon, mayo, roasted tomatoes
Sausage, turkey bacon, egg, tomato relish
Portobello mushroom, egg, spinach, caramelized onion
Swiss cheese croissant: egg, turkey ham, tomato
Smashed avocado on rye: smoked bresaola, quail egg, fennel dill salad
Egg and bacon rolls: beef or turkey bacon
Spinach, mushroom, grilled halloumi pesto wrap
Vegetarian frittata wrap: roasted peppers and feta
Cheese and tomato sandwich in brown bread
Boiled egg, mayonnaise and mustard cress sandwich in multi-cereal bread
Brunch salads and the grazing table
Where brunch runs into lunch, the salads carry it. The strongest menus in the city run six to eighteen here, and (V) is marked item by item, not buried in a footnote at the bottom.
Grilled Mediterranean vegetables (V): Persian feta, pesto, baby herb salad
Cauliflower and quinoa (V): roasted fig, pomegranate, labneh, mint, orange blossom dressing
Roasted beetroot salad (V): peaches, white asparagus, savory granola, cinnamon basil, verjuice
Middle Eastern scented pilaf: raisins, coconut, coriander, honey, cumin vinaigrette
Heirloom tomato (V): Asiago cheese, olive soil, house vinaigrette
Caesar: garlic encroute, quail eggs, turkey bacon, white anchovies
Tuna niçoise: heirloom tomatoes, olives, chat potatoes, white anchovies
Pickled carrot and pearl barley (V): dates, raisins, Arabic aromatics, pine nuts, candied hibiscus, zaatar lemon vinaigrette
Cheese platter: cheddar and blue cheese
Standing brunch — canapés and finger food

For a launch morning or a press brunch where nobody sits down, the same kitchen swaps plates for finger food catering dubai hosts can eat with a drink in the other hand. Five to ten cold and six to eight hot is the usual split.
Asparagus and poached quail egg (V): Taleggio, baguette en croute
Smoked salmon blini: sour cream and chive, pickled gherkin, mustard cress
Cured mackerel: pickled fennel, horseradish crème fraiche, poppy-seed bagel
Wagyu beef cannoli: beetroot, spiced ricotta, baby herbs, sumac thyme sea salt
Pumpkin, spinach and mascarpone scones (V): oven roasted tomatoes
Pumpkin and sage calzone: semi dried tomatoes, buffalo mozzarella, basil
Rolled omelette: wilted spinach, sausage, roasted tomato
Smoked chicken apple sausage and egg slider
Shawarma breakfast pies: roasted tomato, spinach, pancetta, egg
Sri Lankan egg hoppers (V): green sambal, split peas, sauté kale, coconut gel
Big breakfast waffle: wilted spinach, sausage, roasted tomato
Chicken waffle: pickled fennel, roquette, lemon, dill, seeded mustard dressing
Live stations, cooked in front of your guests
Two to four stations is the usual booking, and the point is the interaction as much as the food — a chef works each one for the whole service. The ones we arrange most often for brunch:
Live egg and omelette station: plain, cheese, mushroom, turkey ham, beef bacon, cooked to order
Live crepe station, sweet and savoury: Nutella, strawberry, banana, olives, grilled vegetables, assorted cheeses
Pancake station with a toppings bar
Live saj / manakish station: dough rolled and baked to order on the dome
Live dosa and idli counter: worked by a South Indian specialist
Luqaimat and regag station: fried and syruped in front of the table
Coffee and juice bar: manned barista counter

A station only goes into your proposal once the equipment and the chef who works it are confirmed with the assigned culinary partner for your date. We leave a station off the page before we put one on a quote we cannot staff.
Three tiers, one stand per two guests, and a takeaway version if the party is moving on. The bottom tier is four to six sandwich varieties, cut fine and halved on the platter.
Roast smoked beef with caramelised onion
Two or three scone types plus three accompaniments. This tier is close to fixed across the market, and that is the point of it.
High tea — the sweet tier and petit fours
Six to ten items on the top tier, and this is where a pastry chef either shows or does not.
Cherry, rose water and hazelnut nougat
Matcha choux buns: craquelin topping, vanilla yuzu custard
Arabic high tea — the Traditional Set
There is a local answer to the three-tier stand, and plenty of hosts prefer it. Five to seven items, served against the International Set, not in place of it.
Where brunch runs past midday, four to six of these close the table.
Chocolate thyme pancakes: maple syrup ice cream, honey handkerchiefs
Chocolate truffle waffle: vanilla Chantilly, stone fruit compote
Apple and rosemary salted caramel: candied orange, brioche
Fruit skewer: elderflower jelly and gold leaf
Dietary options across the brunch menu

Halal is the default across every section, and the Western items are specified accordingly — turkey bacon, beef bacon, chicken sausage, turkey ham. Vegetarian dishes are marked (V) item by item, and there is a full plant-based line: coconut yoghurt, nut milks, vegan baked goods, the green morning bowl and the vegetable-led salads.

Gluten-free, nut-conscious and other dietary menu options may be available on request, subject to confirmation by the assigned culinary partner. Partner kitchens may handle allergens, and cross-contact cannot be completely excluded unless dedicated controls have been specifically confirmed for the booking. Guests with allergies must provide full details before confirming their event.
Formats, minimums and how far ahead to book

The same menu is served several different ways, and the format is usually the first thing to settle: a hot chafing line with a cold bakery table for 30 or more; a lighter continental credenza for a boardroom morning; individual boxes labelled per guest; a grab-and-go counter by the door; drop-off platters sized by persons served; a grazing spread; a 30-to-45-minute coffee-break format for a training day; a bowl-and-fork standing brunch with no seating; or plated service running three to seven courses.

Volume formats start at 10 guests, or 20 for a full buffet, with a minimum order value of AED 900. A staffed private-chef brunch is priced per head and carries no minimum headcount, so a six-person family table is a real booking. For context on those numbers: Elements asks 20 guests on a buffet, Al Safadi catering asks 30 on every buffet package, and Taste Studio takes business-lunch delivery from 10 people.

On timing, our preferred lead times are 48 hours for a standard private-chef brunch, 72 hours for a standard catering package, 3–5 days once live stations or multiple staff are involved, 5–7 days for a bespoke menu or a larger private event, and 7–14 days or more for a wedding or a complex production. We recommend booking as early as possible. Lead times depend on guest numbers, menu complexity, staffing, equipment, location and partner availability. Tight timeline for your brunch? We check live partner availability before saying yes or no.

add_block.new_heading: How does brunch service, styling and setup work?
new_paragraphs: Most brunches run as a buffet or live stations, though we shape the format around your venue, guest count and the look you want. Plated service suits a seated wedding brunch; grazing tables and stations suit a flowing party. Styling matters at brunch — daylight is honest — so your chef plates on considered boards, tiered stands and fresh linen, with the food as the centrepiece. For a garden, rooftop or poolside setting we plan for heat and shade; for luxury brunch catering dubai in a villa or penthouse we bring front-of-house polish to match the room. One team handles cooking, service, setup and cleanup from arrival to the last cleared glass.

add_block.new_heading: How to hire brunch catering in Dubai
new_paragraphs: To hire brunch catering dubai, send us the date, guest count and venue, and we typically reply within 15 minutes during business hours. From there it is three steps: we propose a tailored menu and a fixed quote; you confirm and we lock your chef and staff; on the day the team arrives early, sets up, cooks, serves and cleans. Looking for brunch catering near me means matching you with a private brunch chef dubai already working in your area, so travel and sourcing stay efficient. A week's notice is comfortable for a small gathering; book earlier for large parties, weekends and peak dates. Whether you want a one-off or the best brunch catering dubai for a recurring event, the process is the same and the price is clear before you commit.

add_block.new_heading: Planning brunch catering step by step
new_paragraphs: Send your date, guest count and venue — your proposal arrives.

Book brunch catering on our preferred lead times — 72 hours for a standard package, 3–5 days once live stations are involved. This is guidance, not a fixed rule; short-notice requests are assessed individually.
Confirm the menu 7 days before the date, with final numbers.
Ask about allergies when booking, well outside the final 48 hours .
Check how the team reaches the venue; setup begins about 2 hours before guests.
Plan on roughly 3 hours of service, and add 5% VAT to the total.
